examples.problem: Let $A$ be a $2\times 2$ matrix such that $\textrm{tr}(A)=-4$ and $\textrm{det}(A)=-18.$ If $A^2 = xA + yI$ for constants $x$ and $y,$ then find the value of $x+y.$
examples.worked_solution:
The characteristic polynomial of $A$ is given by 

$$
p(\lambda)=\lambda^2-\textrm{tr}(A)\lambda+\textrm{det}(A).
$$

Therefore, using the Cayley-Hamilton theorem, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}p(A) & =O \\ {A}^{2}-\text{tr}(A)A+\text{det}(A)I & =O \\ {A}^{2} & =\text{tr}(A)A-\text{det}(A)I \\ {A}^{2} & =-4A+18I.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $x+y = -4+18 = 14.$

feedback.problem: Given that $A=[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{2} & \frac{5}{2} \\ \frac{7}{5} & -2\end{aligned}],$ find the product of the eigenvalues of $A.$
feedback.worked_solution:
The characteristic polynomial of $A$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}p(\lambda ) & ={\lambda }^{2}-\text{tr}(A)\lambda +\text{det}(A).\end{aligned}
$$

Now, using Vieta's Formulas, we have that the roots of $p(\lambda ),$ i.e. the eigenvalues of $A,$ satisfy

$$
{\begin{aligned}{\lambda }_{1}+{\lambda }_{2}=\text{tr}(A) \\ {\lambda }_{1}\cdot {\lambda }_{2}=\text{det}(A).\end{aligned}
$$

So, the product of the eigenvalues of $A$ is equal to the determinant of $A.$ Therefore, 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\lambda }_{1}\cdot {\lambda }_{2} & =det(A) \\  & =|\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{2} & \frac{5}{2} \\ \frac{7}{5} & -2\end{aligned}| \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot (-2)-\frac{5}{2}\cdot \frac{7}{5} \\  & =-1-\frac{7}{2} \\  & =-\frac{9}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
